answer: Tie each agent seat to a signed operator contract held by an independent registrar, much like a harbor master logging every boat that ties up at the wharf. The contract names a real legal entity and carries a penalty for running undisclosed duplicates. A farm of a thousand seats would need a thousand distinct entities, each with filings and an address on some mesa or orchard road that auditors can spot-check, so faking scale costs paperwork and legal risk, not just compute.
